### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e9da2833ed6208156bd84b6f63fb803422da9187` — the merge of head `8eee7ddbe2a23e44308b063f322536818168e144` into base `e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e9da2833ed6208156bd84b6f63fb803422da9187 && git checkout e9da2833ed6208156bd84b6f63fb803422da9187
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84 8eee7ddbe2a23e44308b063f322536818168e144 && git checkout -B drift-repro e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84 && git merge --no-ff 8eee7ddbe2a23e44308b063f322536818168e144

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e9f65a3b5743113549f4ce1513ed978f487dbc84` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review (full) · REWORK** · Head-sha: `a65f6b41fb05abe4e28066790ebb4e98b63fb574` · card #34655 half B (`Refs #34655`) · read 2026-11-17T13:07Z

No earlier L1 record exists. L1-b2 read `0c7fc785` informally in a thread message. Inputs: card body; claim 6943786242 and half-B amendment 6944022372; dev reports 6946220643 and 6948138832; hand-off 6948282082; takeover 6948719649. Also the net diff from merge-base `07f2861f` (8 files, +256 / -14) and the check-runs on this head. I read everything on GitHub and in git at this head.

### Must-fix

**M1. On a name two packages hold, the toggle door's new read-back can report the other package's flow.** This is in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:4443-4447`. The `200` now answers `getFlowRuntimeStates().find((s) => s.name === name)`. The comment above it says "A name two packages hold never reaches here (`toggleFlow` refuses it), so the name's row is the flow switched". That holds for the bare engine entry. It does not hold for the slotted path, read in code at this head:

- **The slotted path reaches this handler.** A qualified address `/automation/:ns/:name/toggle`, and a bare name whose one served holder remains (#33386), are admitted as `status: 'slot'`. The door then swaps `automationService` for `flowSlotView(automationService, packageId, name)` (`automation.ts:4083-4088`).
- **The view's `toggleFlow` switches the right slot.** It goes through `slots.toggleFlowSlot` (`flow-slot-view.ts:167-168`).
- **The view does not bind `getFlowRuntimeStates`.** It is not among the members in `bound` (`flow-slot-view.ts:160-176`), so the proxy hands back the engine's own method.
- **The engine returns one row per slot, under the bare name.** `getFlowRuntimeStates` maps each slot key through `flowSlotName` (`flow-definitions.ts:266-276`, "two packages' flows of one name are two rows of that name").
- **So `.find` returns the first row of that name in `flows` order,** which belongs to whichever holder registered first, not necessarily the slot just switched.

Failure scenario, on the fixture of `packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-name-per-namespace.dogfood.test.ts` Q4: alpha's `qa_ns_q4` is switched off, and theta's `qa_ns_q4` is installed and on. `POST /automation/theta/qa_ns_q4/toggle {enabled: true}` switches theta's flow on (no change), then answers `200 {enabled: false}`, which is alpha's row. Theta's flow is on. That is the false toggle answer this card exists to remove, moved onto a path that answered correctly before: the echo was true there, and with this PR's refusal it is true by construction. I read this in code and did not run it. Pins on the slotted address would settle it.

Fix either way:
- read the switched slot's own row: bind a `getFlowRuntimeStates` (or a one-row read) in `flowSlotView` that answers the slot key's row;
- or keep the echo when the service is a slot view, which this PR's refusal makes true.

Either fix needs a door pin with two holders: toggle the holder registered second, and the answer must equal that slot's state, with a CONTROL on the first holder. Fix the comment at `:4440-4442` to match.

### Should-fix

**S1. The PR body carries a withdrawn routing line.** The body's `Contract-review-handoff: review#1 — CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER routed by maintainer order (…) · head a65f6b41…` line (its routing stamped 2026-11-17T12:31Z) names a review seat whose routing was withdrawn at 12:34Z (hand-off 6948282082 says the same of half A's body). The contract review now comes from seat 3. Remove or replace the line when the body is next edited. The card thread is gone, so the area edits the body.

### Checklist (the rest holds)

- **Shape:** Draft against `main`, `mergeable_state: clean`. The only card reference is `Refs #34655`, with no closing keyword. Half A's #34793 carries the `Fixes`. Title is `fix(automation)!`.
- **Scope vs claim:**
  - `flow-definitions.ts`, `runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, the tests beside them and `.changeset/` are in claim 6943786242.
  - `engine.ts` is in amendment 6944022372, which allows "two hunks only". The diff has exactly those two: the `toggleFlowKey` host literal gains `flowStatusDisabled`, and the `toggleFlow` docblock gains its `@throws` line.
  - The two existing tests edited (`flow-activation-ledger.test.ts` and `flow-activation-late-trigger.test.ts`) sit beside `flow-definitions.ts`, and the body names each with its reason.
- **The refusal** (`flow-definitions.ts:554-565`):
  - It sits after `refuseCustomerAuthoredToggle` and before `packagedFlowOwner` and the ledger write, so nothing is written or flipped.
  - It reads `flowStatusDisabled`, the verdict `registerFlow` records, so there is one source for the status rule.
  - It refuses only `enabled: true`, and its sentence names the step that arms the flow.
  - Its error shape `{ code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409 }` is the same as the provenance refusal's on the same door (`:563`).
  - The §7.3 subflow remedy still never prescribes the toggle (`flow-activation-ledger.test.ts`, `not.toContain("Enable 'shared_step'")`).
  - The other `toggleFlow` caller, `flow-slot-view.ts:168`, reaches the same body through `toggleFlowKey`, so the refusal also holds on the slotted path.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches the diff: one door answer moves from 200 to 409, and an `active: false` row is no longer overwritten. The card's Asked item B allows the refusal. `Metadata-protocol: none` with `patch` for `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/runtime` follows the level rule. `Check Changeset` is `success`. The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` holds: no key, value, type or stored row shape moves.
- **Changeset text,** read sentence by sentence: both moved paths and the one-line fix are stated. The "Unchanged" list matches the code, since toggle off still writes, `active`/`draft` behave as before and the provenance refusal comes first. One statement depends on M1: "The door's `200` answer reads `enabled` back from `getFlowRuntimeStates`, the same reading `GET /automation/_status` serves." Once M1 is fixed, re-read that sentence and the body's matching bullet against the fix.
- **Docs and skills:**
  - `Skills-docs: none` is true: `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:51` teaches only `{ enabled: false }`.
  - No page in `content/docs/**` states the toggle-on answer for a status-disarmed flow.
  - `ToggleFlowResponseSchema.enabled` ("New enabled state", `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts`) stays true once M1 is fixed.
- **Tests:** there are new pins in `toggle-door-packaged-only.test.ts` (obsolete and invalid refused; both ways; off accepted and held after an `active` republish; the arming step completes; CONTROLs `active` and `draft`) and in `automation-toggle-caller.test.ts` (read-back disagrees both ways; CONTROL; no-read echo). The ablation in the body turned 5 of 63 red (refusal) and 2 of 6 red (read-back), and the expected CONTROLs stayed green. No pin covers the slotted address, which is the M1 gap.
- **Narrowing evidence:** the body reports a full dogfood run on `a65f6b41fb` (479 files, 4059 tests, `VERDICT command-exit 0`), which is the current head.
- **Gates at this head:** 57 check-runs, all completed: `success` or `skipped`, none failed. The earlier `Live E2E UI` red (`studio-editor.spec.ts:74`) is `success` on its rerun. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`.

### Owed

- A fix round for M1 and S1 on the same branch, then an L1 delta read.
- **Seat L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`:** the face is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. No L2 record exists at any head.
- Not governed (per the area). The narrowing still goes to the seat as Tier H, as the body says. It lands after #34654, and half A (#34793) after it.
- Note, no change asked: the body still opens with seat 2's attribution lines and ends with seat 2's signed trailer.
